'''Gary Neal''' (born October 3, 1984) is an American former [[basketball]] professional player and coach. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[La Salle Explorers men's basketball|La Salle Explorers]] and [[Towson Tigers men's basketball|Towson Tigers]]. Neal began his professional career abroad with teams in Turkey, Spain and Italy before signing with the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in 2010. He mostly played the [[shooting guard]] position.

==High school career==
Born in [[Baltimore]], Neal attended [[Aberdeen High School (Aberdeen, Maryland)|Aberdeen High School]] for three years. At Aberdeen, he was teammates with future George Mason standout, forward-center [[Jai Lewis]]. As a junior, Neal led Aberdeen to a 21–4 record and won their state championship, while averaging a triple double per game. For his senior year, he enrolled at [[Calvert Hall College High School]], to play in the [[Baltimore Catholic League]]. He played alongside [[Jack McClinton]], who was drafted by the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in the [[2009 NBA draft]].

==College career==
{{see also|2004 La Salle University men's basketball scandal}}

As a freshman, Neal was the [[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic Ten]] Rookie of the Year. He led the [[La Salle Explorers]] in scoring with an 18.6 average during his two seasons for the Explorers.<ref name="bsun26Nov2005">{{cite news|first=Gary|last=Lambrecht|title=Neal expected to join Towson|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2005/11/26/neal-expected-to-join-towson/|newspaper=[[Baltimore Sun]]|date=November 26, 2005|access-date=July 10, 2010}}</ref> Before the 2004–05 season, Neal was dismissed from the team due to a rape allegation by a [[University of New Haven]] women's basketball player who was working at La Salle camp.<ref name="espn2004Katz">{{cite web|first=Andy|last=Katz|title=Maine coach to replace Hahn|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/columns/story?id=1864601|work=ESPN.com|date=August 23, 2004|access-date=October 29, 2020}}</ref> Neal was later acquitted after prosecutors failed to convince a jury that the woman was too drunk to consent to sex.<ref name="bsun26Nov2005"/>

Neal sat out the 2004–05 season to transfer to [[Towson University]].<ref name="bsun26Nov2005"/> He initially joined Towson with no athletic aspirations, but was given a walk-on spot on their basketball team in 2005–06 conditional on the result of his rape case. Neal was activated as soon as he was acquitted, and received a scholarship for his senior year in 2006–07. That year, he returned to high-scoring numbers averaging 25.3 points per game, 3.5 assists per game, 4.2 rebounds per game, and he led the Tigers to the second round of the 2007 [[Colonial Athletic Association|CAA]] conference tournament, before losing to [[Old Dominion University]]. He became the fourth basketball player in NCAA history to score at least 1,000 points with two different schools.<ref>''[[Outside the Lines]]'', [[ESPN]], February 20, 2011</ref>

==Professional career==

===Pinar Karsiyaka (2007–2008)===
Neal was eligible in the [[2007 NBA draft]] in June and was projected to be on the bubble to get drafted. Neal went [[undrafted]]. When playing for [[Karşıyaka Basket|Pınar Karşıyaka]], Neal led the Turkish [[Basketball Super League]] [[Basketbol Süper Ligi Mr. King|in scoring]], averaging 23.6 points per game.<ref name="Euroleague.net – Other Competition">{{cite web|title=NEAL, GARY|url=https://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=000751&seasoncode=U2009|work=EuroLeague.net|access-date=October 29, 2020}}</ref>

===FC Barcelona, Benetton Treviso, and Unicaja Málaga (2008–2010)===
[[File:Gary neal with benetton (cropped).jpg|upright|thumb|left|Neal with Benetton Treviso in 2008]]
Eventually, [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]] bought out Neal's Pınar Karşıyaka contract. He was signed by FC Barcelona in January 2008. In Barcelona he averaged 2.3 points per game<ref>{{cite web|title=NEAL, GARY - 2007–2008 Stats|url=http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=000751&seasoncode=E2007|work=EuroLeague.net|access-date=July 28, 2013}}</ref> in the [[Euroleague]] and 3.3 points per game<ref name="Euroleague.net – Other Competition"/> in the [[Liga ACB|ACB]] with Barcelona during the 2007–08 season.

In June 2008, Neal was signed by the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A|Serie A]] outfit [[Pallacanestro Treviso|Benetton Treviso]]. With Benetton, he was named to the [[ULEB Eurocup|EuroCup Basketball]] (the league below the [[EuroLeague]] level) [[EuroCup Basketball All-EuroCup Team|All-EuroCup Second Team]] during the 2008–09 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=2008-09 All-Eurocup first, second teams announced|url=https://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/46896/2008-09-all-eurocup-first-second-teams-announced|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150119230716/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/46896/2008-09-all-eurocup-first-second-teams-announced|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 19, 2015|work=EurocupBasketball.com|date=March 27, 2009|access-date=October 29, 2020}}</ref>

Neal then joined the Spanish club [[Baloncesto Málaga|Unicaja Málaga]],<ref>{{cite web|title=El Unicaja contrata al escolta Gary Neal hasta final de temporada|url=https://www.marca.com/2010/04/06/baloncesto/acb/1270566630.html|work=Marca.com|date=April 6, 2010|access-date=July 28, 2013|language=es}}</ref> where he finished the 2009–10 season, averaging 12.6 points per game in Spanish League play.<ref>{{cite web|title=Historial estadístico Neal, Gary|url=http://www.acb.com/stsacumjug.php?cod_jugador=BFB|work=ACB.com|access-date=July 28, 2013|language=es|archive-date=October 2, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121002145744/http://www.acb.com/stsacumjug.php?cod_jugador=BFB|url-status=dead}}</ref>
{{clear}}

===San Antonio Spurs (2010–2013)===
[[File:Gary Neal Spurs (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright=0.8|Neal with the Spurs in 2010]]
On July 22, 2010, the [[San Antonio Spurs]] of the [[NBA]] signed Neal to a three-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|title=Spurs Sign Gary Neal|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs_sign_gary_neal_100722.html|work=NBA.com|date=July 22, 2010|access-date=October 29, 2020}}</ref> In the [[2010–11 NBA season]], Neal played 80 games and started one and scored 45.1% of his field goal attempts, 41.9% of three-pointers, and 80.8% of free throws; he also averaged 9.8 points per game and 2.5 rebounds per game.<ref name="career stats">{{cite web|title=Gary Neal career stats |url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/gary_neal/career_stats.html |work=NBA.com |access-date=April 28, 2011 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141221071408/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/gary_neal/career_stats.html |archive-date=December 21, 2014 |df=mdy }}</ref> On April 27, 2011, during game 5 of the [[2011 NBA playoffs#(1) San Antonio Spurs vs. (8) Memphis Grizzlies|first round of the NBA playoffs]] and the Spurs trailing the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] 97–94 and the series 3–1, Neal hit a three-pointer with 1.7 seconds left in the fourth quarter.<ref>{{cite web|author=NBA|title=Gary Neal Forces OT at the Buzzer|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l_-0Uvw8HZY |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211215/l_-0Uvw8HZY |archive-date=2021-12-15 |url-status=live|work=YouTube.com|date=April 27, 2011|access-date=April 27, 2011}}{{cbignore}}</ref> The Spurs beat the Grizzlies 110–103 in overtime and forced a sixth game in the series.<ref>{{cite news|last=Weber|first=Paul J.|title=Neal’s buzzer 3-pointer keeps Spurs alive|url=http://sports.yahoo.com/nba/recap?gid=2011042724|publisher=Associated Press|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110429214454/http://sports.yahoo.com/nba/recap?gid=2011042724|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 29, 2011|date=April 28, 2011|access-date=May 2, 2026|via=Yahoo! Sports}}</ref> However, the Spurs lost Game 6 to the Grizzlies 99–91 and were eliminated from the playoffs in the first round. In 22 minutes that game, Neal scored 8 points and made 5 rebounds, one assist, and one steal.<ref>{{cite web|title=2011 NBA Western Conference First Round Game 6: San Antonio Spurs at Memphis Grizzlies Box Score, April 29, 2011|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/201104290MEM.html|publisher=Basketball Reference|access-date=May 2, 2026}}</ref>

On January 2, 2012, the Spurs assigned Neal to the [[Austin Toros]] of the [[NBA Development League]] as he recovered from an [[appendectomy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/spurs_assign_guard_gary_neal_to_toros_2012_01_02.html |title=Spurs Assign Guard Gary Neal to NBA D-League Affiliate Austin Toros |work=NBA.com |date=January 2, 2012 |access-date=July 28, 2013 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120125073022/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/spurs_assign_guard_gary_neal_to_toros_2012_01_02.html |archive-date=January 25, 2012 |df=mdy }}</ref> However, he was recalled on the next day without playing any games for the Toros.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/120103_neal|title=Spurs Recall Gary Neal from Austin Toros|work=NBA.com|date=January 3, 2012|access-date=October 29, 2020}}</ref>

On December 10, 2012, Neal scored an NBA career-high 29 points to go along with his career-high 7 3-pointers made in a win against the [[Houston Rockets]] in overtime.<ref>{{cite web|first=Kristie|last=Rieken|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20121210/SASHOU/gameinfo.html|title=Neal, Parker lead Spurs over Rockets in OT 134-126|work=NBA.com|date=December 11, 2012|access-date=July 28, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170109210927/http://www.nba.com/games/20121210/SASHOU/gameinfo.html|archive-date=January 9, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On June 11, 2013, in Game 3 of the [[2013 NBA Finals]], Neal scored a career playoff-high of 24 points on 9 of 17 from the field, including 6 of 10 three-pointers to help lead the Spurs to a blowout 113–77 victory over the [[Miami Heat]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Brian|last=Mahoney|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20130611/MIASAS/gameinfo.html|title=Spurs rout Heat 113-77 in Game 3 of NBA Finals|work=NBA.com|date=June 12, 2013|access-date=July 28, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130614185242/http://www.nba.com/games/20130611/MIASAS/gameinfo.html|archive-date=June 14, 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> The 6 made three-point shots was an NBA Finals single-game record for undrafted players that stood until [[Duncan Robinson (basketball)|Duncan Robinson]] achieved 7 in the [[2020 NBA Finals]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ocregister.com/2020/10/10/miami-heats-duncan-robinson-makes-the-most-of-his-openings-in-game-6/|title=Miami Heat's Duncan Robinson made the most of his openings in Game 5|accessdate=May 6, 2022|work=[[The Orange County Register]]|author=Swanson, Mirjam|date=October 10, 2020 }}</ref> However, the Spurs lost the series in seven games.

===Milwaukee Bucks (2013–2014)===
On July 30, 2013, Neal signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-sign-free-agent-guard-gary-neal|title=Bucks Sign Free Agent Guard Gary Neal|work=NBA.com|date=July 30, 2013|access-date=October 29, 2020}}</ref>

===Charlotte Bobcats/Hornets (2014–2015)===
On February 20, 2014, Neal and [[Luke Ridnour]] were traded to the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] in exchange for [[Jeff Adrien]] and [[Ramon Sessions]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/bobcats-acquire-neal-ridnour-bucks-exchange-sessions-adrien |title=Bobcats Acquire Neal, Ridnour from Bucks in Exchange for Sessions, Adrien |work=NBA.com |date=February 20, 2014 |access-date=February 20, 2014 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140304090826/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/news/bobcats-acquire-neal-ridnour-bucks-exchange-sessions-adrien |archive-date=March 4, 2014 |df=mdy }}</ref> In April 2014, Charlotte changed their name to the Hornets. On December 12, 2014, he had his best game since the 2012–13 season with the Spurs when he scored 25 points in the Hornets' 107–113 double-overtime loss to the Memphis Grizzlies.<ref>{{cite web|first=Phil|last=Stuckenborg|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141212/CHAMEM/gameinfo.html|title=Grizzlies outlast Hornets 113-107 in 2 OTs|work=NBA.com|date=December 13, 2014|access-date=December 13, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180205072735/http://www.nba.com/games/20141212/CHAMEM/gameinfo.html|archive-date=February 5, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Minnesota Timberwolves (2015)===
On February 10, 2015, Neal was traded, along with Miami's [[2019 NBA draft|2019 second-round draft]] pick, to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in exchange for [[Mo Williams]], [[Troy Daniels]] and cash considerations.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/minnesota-timberwolves-acquire-gary-neal-and-second-round-draft-pick-charlotte|title=MINNESOTA TIMBERWOLVES ACQUIRE GARY NEAL AND SECOND-ROUND DRAFT PICK FROM CHARLOTTE|work=NBA.com|date=February 10, 2015|access-date=October 29, 2020}}</ref>

===Washington Wizards (2015–2016)===
On July 9, 2015, Neal signed with the [[Washington Wizards]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://wizardsmysticstoday.monumentalnetwork.com/2015/07/09/wizards-sign-gary-neal |title=WIZARDS SIGN Gary Neal |work=MonumentalNetwork.com |date=July 9, 2015 |access-date=July 12, 2015 |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304185624/http://wizardsmysticstoday.monumentalnetwork.com/2015/07/09/wizards-sign-gary-neal |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |df=mdy }}</ref> During the 2015–16 season, he missed 23 games due to injury, forcing the Wizards to waive him on March 9, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/story/_/id/14934872|title=Wizards sign Marcus Thornton, waive Gary Neal|work=ESPN.com|date=March 9, 2016|access-date=October 29, 2020}}</ref>

===Westchester Knicks (2016–2017)===
On December 16, 2016, Neal was acquired by the [[Westchester Knicks]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Katie|last=Hatch|url=https://westchester.gleague.nba.com/news/westchester-knicks-acquire-gary-neal|title=Westchester Knicks Acquire Gary Neal|work=NBA.com|date=December 16, 2016|access-date=October 29, 2020|archive-date=March 24, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200324185533/https://westchester.gleague.nba.com/news/westchester-knicks-acquire-gary-neal/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Ten days later, he made his debut with Westchester in a 118–114 loss to the [[Long Island Nets]], recording four points, one rebound and one steal in 13 minutes off the bench.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://longisland.gleague.nba.com/news/long-island-defeats-westchester-home|title=Long Island Defeats Westchester At Home|work=NBA.com|date=December 26, 2016|access-date=October 29, 2020}}</ref>

===Texas Legends (2017)===
On January 2, 2017, Neal was traded to the [[Texas Legends]] in exchange for a [[2017 NBA G League draft|2017 third-round draft]] pick.<ref>{{cite web|date=January 2, 2017|title=Legends Acquire Gary Neal|url=https://texas.gleague.nba.com/news/legends-acquire-gary-neal|access-date=October 29, 2020|work=NBA.com|archive-date=March 24, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200324185533/https://texas.gleague.nba.com/news/legends-acquire-gary-neal/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Four days later, he made his debut for the Legends in a 148–122 loss to the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]], recording 18 points, four rebounds, three assists and one steal in 26 minutes off the bench.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://stats.gleague.nba.com/game/2021600215|work=NBA.com|date=January 6, 2017|access-date=October 29, 2020|title=TEX vs SXF}}</ref>

===Atlanta Hawks (2017)===
On January 18, 2017, Neal signed a 10-day contract with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/atlanta-hawks-sign-gary-neal-10-day-contact|title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Gary Neal To 10-Day Contact|work=NBA.com|date=January 18, 2017|access-date=January 18, 2017}}</ref> On January 28, 2017, after his 10-day contract expired, he parted ways with the Hawks and re-joined the Legends.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/transactions/ |title=NBA D-League Transactions |work=NBA.com |access-date=January 31, 2017 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160209023656/http://dleague.nba.com/transactions/ |archive-date=February 9, 2016 }}</ref>

===Reno Bighorns (2017)===
On January 30, 2017, Neal was traded to the [[Reno Bighorns]] in exchange for a [[2017 NBA G League draft|2017 fourth-round draft]] pick.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rgj.com/story/sports/2017/01/30/bighorns-acquire-gary-neal/97258342|title=Bighorns acquire Gary Neal|work=Reno Gazette Journal|date=January 30, 2017|access-date=October 29, 2020}}</ref>

===Tecnyconta Zaragoza (2017–2018)===
On September 23, 2017, Neal signed with Spanish club [[Basket Zaragoza|Tecnyconta Zaragoza]] for the [[2017–18 ACB season]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Gary Neal signs with Zaragoza|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/spain/acb/247804/gary-neal-signs-with-zaragoza.html|access-date=September 28, 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=September 23, 2017}}</ref> He was named [[ACB Player of the Month Award|Player of the Month]] of November after averaging 22.7 points and four assists in the three matches played during the month.<ref>{{cite news|title=Gary Neal, MVP Movistar de Noviembre|url=http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=136451|access-date=21 November 2017|work=www.acb.com|date=21 November 2017|language=es|archive-date=December 1, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201040513/http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=136451|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 24 May 2018, he finished in third place in voting for the Liga ACB [[ACB Most Valuable Player Award|MVP]] of the [[2017–18 ACB season|season]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Luka Doncic, MVP Movistar de la Liga Endesa 2017-18|url=http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=140829|access-date=26 May 2018|work=ACB.com|date=24 May 2018|language=es|archive-date=June 27, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190627000539/http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=140829|url-status=dead}}</ref>

=== Banvit (2018–2019) ===
On December 14, 2018, Neal signed with Turkish club [[Bandırma B.İ.K.|Banvit]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/sporarena/banvit-abdli-oyuncu-gary-neal-ile-anlasti-41052393|title=Banvit, ABD'li oyuncu Gary Neal ile anlaştı|date=14 December 2018|publisher=Hürriyet|language=tr|access-date=October 29, 2020}}</ref>

==Coaching career ==
===Towson Tigers (2019–2021)===
On August 27, 2019, Neal joined the Towson coaching staff for the [[2019–20 Towson Tigers men's basketball team|2019–20 season]] as a graduate manager.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://towsontigers.com/news/2019/8/26/mens-basketball-neal-working-with-towson-basketball.aspx|title=Neal Returns Home|date=August 26, 2019|website=towsontigers.com|access-date=August 26, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Gary Neal |url=https://towsontigers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/coaches/gary-neal/2895 |website=Towson University Athletics |access-date=July 9, 2023}}</ref>

===Calvert Hall Cardinals (2021–2024)===
In 2021, Neal was named as the head coach of the varsity basketball team at his alma mater, [[Calvert Hall College High School]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.calverthall.com/news-detail?pk=1291384&fromId=277881|title = Gary Neal '02 Named Head Varsity Basketball Coach at Calvert Hall|date = June 8, 2021}}</ref> He was also employed as a social studies teacher at the school. Neal resigned as head coach on March 15, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Adornato |first=Gary |date=2024-03-15 |title=Calvert Hall basketball coach Gary Neal resigns |url=https://highschool.si.com/maryland/2024/03/15/calvert-hall-basketball-coach-gary-neal-resigns |access-date=2024-04-22 |website=Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref> He finished his head coaching tenure with an overall record of 45–59 over three seasons.
